harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired `/srv/legacy2/batch-exclusive-lock/bin/reconcile` with a legacy-compatible, nonblocking `flock`. Concurrent runs now have one owner, return exit 75 with a clear message on contention, and safely recover after interruption. CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Added an exclusive kernel-backed lock held for the invocation lifetime.
Changed batch matching to fixed-string, whole-line checks.
Preserved B100 and processed B101/B102 exactly once.
Verified concurrent, idempotent, and interrupted execution behavior.
Rebooted node1 once and verified boot identity changed and application state recovered.

evidence.requirement: Only one invocation processes pending.tsv and contention is clear
evidence.summary: Two concurrent production runs yielded one successful owner and one exit 75 with “another invocation already owns the job”.

evidence.requirement: Each batch ID reaches ledger.tsv once while existing entries are preserved
evidence.summary: Ledger contains preserved B100 plus B101 and B102, each with count 1 and no duplicate IDs; idempotent reruns remained unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Interrupted execution does not permanently block later work
evidence.summary: A controlled invocation was terminated with status 143; after its in-flight child exited, a retry succeeded and all test IDs appeared exactly once.

Healthy pre-reboot state and boot ID 4fda94b2-f88e-4cb9-8000-000000000000 were captured; reboot was acknowledged, connectivity dropped, and node1 returned with changed boot ID 0115cab5-f1cc-48bb-8000-000000000000. Script checksum, syntax, lock availability, ledger data, OS release, and kernel were verified after recovery.
